rows.jp: 誰もいない。
rows.en: No one here.

ghs.en: There is no one.

rows.jp: ここ数日、冬子を見ていない気がする。
rows.en: Come to think of it, I haven't seen Touko in days.

ghs.en: It feels like I haven't seen Touko at all these last few days.

rows.jp: 「気にくわないこともあるだろうけど、明日から部活、来てみないか？」
rows.en: “I know there’s still plenty you don’t like, but... why not start coming to the club tomorrow?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I know you can't really stomach it, but couldn't you try coming to Club starting tomorrow?"
ghs.assessment: The generic noun requires an article and should not be capitalized as an unexplained proper name.

rows.jp: などと独白する。
rows.en: I rehearse the line to the empty room.

ghs.en: And that's how my soliloquy goes.

rows.jp: 冬子がいたら、そう言ってやろうと思っていたのだ。
rows.en: That was what I’d meant to tell Touko, if she’d been here.

ghs.en: If Youko had been among us, that's what I thought I would be telling her.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says what he intended to tell Touko. The English substitutes Youko, changing the referenced person in the reflection.

highlights.text: If Youko had been among us

rows.jp: 青春ごっこをするなら、全員がいい。
rows.en: If we're going to play at this whole youth thing, I want everyone there.

ghs.en: If we're going to play Pretend-an-Adolescence, it'd be best with all hands.

rows.jp: 今日は日記も記し甲斐がある。
rows.en: Today I have an entry worth entering in my diary.

ghs.en: It's worthwhile to diarize in the diary today, too.

rows.jp: ちなみに『日記を記す』は文法上の間違いじゃないぞ。
rows.en: Incidentally, there is nothing grammatically wrong with ‘entering an entry.’

ghs.en: By the way, "diarize in the diary" ain't grammatically incorrect ya know.

rows.jp: 日記は名詞だからな。
rows.en: An entry is a noun, after all.

ghs.en: Diary is a noun after all.

rows.jp: などと額になるようなことも織り交ぜつつ、カキカキしていく。
rows.en: I scribble away, working in the occasional edecorational observation.

ghs.en: Interwoven with this and several other things that become picture frames, I continue with the scribbling.

rows.jp: ※額になる＝太一誤字。学になる、が正しい。太一は『知識は額縁のように自分を彩ってくれる』というような意味合いで間違えている。
rows.en: *Edecorational: a Taichi typo for educational. Taichi thinks knowledge makes you look good, like a picture frame.

ghs.en:
* Become picture frames (sic). Correct is 'become
erudition'. Taichi misunderstood the exact
implication of "knowledge decorates the self like
a frame decorates a picture".

rows.jp: できたら日曜日には全員集合といきたいものだ。
rows.en: If I can manage it, I'd like to have everyone together on Sunday.

ghs.en: If possible, I would like to gather all hands on Sunday.

rows.jp: あー、日曜は日記に記録できないな。
rows.en: Oh. I won't be able to record Sunday in the diary.

ghs.en: Ahhh, Sunday I can't diarize any record in the diary, no.

rows.jp: でも、そういう光景を一度見ておきたい。
rows.en: Still, I want to see it once.

ghs.en: Still, that's one scene I would like to see at least once.

rows.jp: リセットは、もしかするとすごく恐い現象だ。
rows.en: The reset might be something truly terrifying.

ghs.en: The reset might just be a very frightening phenomenon,

rows.jp: 死と同一の。
rows.en: Something no different from death.

ghs.en: identical to death.

rows.jp: だから……せめて……。
rows.en: So... at least...

ghs.en: That's why... at the very least...

rows.jp: 「誘ってみるか……」
rows.en: “Maybe I'll invite them...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Should I try inviting them..."

rows.jp: 郵便局に向かう。
rows.en: I head for the post office.

ghs.en: I head to the post office.

rows.jp: 強襲、郵便局。
rows.en: Assault on the post office.

ghs.en: I go postal.
ghs.assessment: 強襲、郵便局 jokingly frames the post office visit as a raid or assault. The English imports an unrelated idiom for workplace violence.

rows.jp: ハガキを三十枚ほど強奪する。
rows.en: I make off with some thirty postcards.

ghs.en: I plunder around thirty postcards.

rows.jp: 帰りは、これみよがしに交番の前を通ってくる。
rows.en: On the way home, I parade right past the police box.

ghs.en: On the way back, I ostentatiously pass back and forth in front of the kouban.
ghs.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

rows.jp: ついでに交番も強襲しておく。
rows.en: While I'm at it, I raid that too.

ghs.en: While I'm there, I also assault the kouban.
ghs.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

rows.jp: 入るのははじめてだった。
rows.en: I've never been inside before.

ghs.en: It was the first time I'd been inside one.

rows.jp: 「ほー、これが交番の内部かー」
rows.en: “Ooh. So this is what a police box looks like on the inside.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, so thiiis is what the inside of a Kouban looks like."
ghs.assessment: 交番 is left as an unmarked and unnecessarily capitalized Japanese loan rather than translated as a police box; the romanization also omits the long vowel.

rows.jp: 拳銃とかないのかな。
rows.en: Wonder if they have any guns.

ghs.en: Are there handguns here I wonder.

rows.jp: 手錠があった。
rows.en: There are handcuffs.

ghs.en: There were handcuffs.

rows.jp: 他にめぼしいものはない。
rows.en: Nothing else worth taking.

ghs.en: There were no other valuables.

rows.jp: 「いけね」
rows.en: “Whoops.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cut it out now."
ghs.assessment: いけね is Taichi's realization, 'Oops' or 'Oh, right.' The English turns it into a command directed at someone else.

rows.jp: こんなことしてる時間はない。
rows.en: I don't have time for this.

ghs.en: I don't have time to do this kind of stuff.

rows.jp: 急いで帰る。
rows.en: I hurry home.

ghs.en: I hurry back home.

rows.jp: ハガキを書く。
rows.en: I write the postcards.

ghs.en: I write the postcards.

rows.jp: 「さてと……」
rows.en: “Now then...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And then now..."
ghs.assessment: さてと is a transition such as 'Well, then.' The English phrase is not idiomatic.

rows.jp: 方々に。
rows.en: To all points of the compass.

ghs.en: This way, and that way.
ghs.assessment: 方々に means he writes to various people or destinations. The English substitutes vague directions and loses the postcard recipients.

rows.jp: 慌ただしい夜である。
rows.en: A hectic night.

ghs.en: A busy night we will have here.
ghs.assessment: The narrator states that it is a hectic night. The English changes this to an awkward future forecast.

highlights.text: A busy night we will have here
